name: OCD Support
description: Support for navigating intrusive thoughts, compulsive behaviours, and the anxiety cycles associated with obsessive-compulsive patterns.

immediateActions.title: Intrusive Thought Awareness Check
instructions: When an intrusive thought arrives, pause and mentally label it: This is an OCD thought
Say silently: This thought is not a fact, it is a signal from my brain that I can observe without acting on
Rate your current anxiety from 0 to 10 and note it
Remind yourself: Having a thought does not mean I want it, agree with it, or will act on it
Continue with whatever you were doing, allowing the thought to be there without pushing it away
After 5 minutes, re-rate your anxiety and notice any change

immediateActions.title: Urge Surfing Coping Technique
instructions: When you feel the urge to perform a compulsion, pause instead of acting immediately
Notice where in your body you feel the urge: tightness, restlessness, warmth, tension
Imagine the urge is a wave that will rise, peak, and then fall on its own
Take slow breaths: in for 4, hold for 2, out for 6
Keep your attention on your breath and the physical sensation without fighting it
Stay with the wave until it passes; most urges peak within 10-15 minutes

immediateActions.title: Ritual Delay and Awareness Log
instructions: When you notice you are about to perform a ritual or compulsion, pause for 10 seconds
Write down: What thought triggered this? What feeling am I trying to reduce?
See if you can delay the ritual by 2 minutes; set a timer and wait
During the delay, breathe slowly and notice the discomfort without judging it
After 2 minutes, decide mindfully: will I proceed, or can I wait another minute?
Whether you delayed or not, note what happened afterwards in your log

immediateActions.title: Understanding OCD Cycle: Break It Down
instructions: Write the trigger that started this cycle: a thought, image, feeling, or situation
Write the obsession (the intrusive thought or doubt that followed)
Write the anxiety or discomfort you felt next and its intensity 0-10
Write the compulsion or avoidance behaviour you used to try to feel better
Write how you felt immediately after: relief, shame, doubt, urge to repeat?
Recognise the cycle and remind yourself: the compulsion strengthens the obsession over time; I can choose to respond differently

tools.name: Cycle Tracker Log
tools.description: Structured log to map triggers, obsessions, compulsions, and anxiety levels over time.

tools.name: Urge Surf Timer
tools.description: Visual timer with guided breathing to help ride out urges with anxiety level re-rating.

tools.name: Self-Talk Scripts
tools.description: Collection of evidence-based scripts to say aloud or silently when intrusive thoughts strike.

tools.name: Graded Challenge Builder
tools.description: Tool to create personalised exposure hierarchies with progress tracking.

tools.name: Mindful Acceptance Audio
tools.description: Guided audio exercises to practice accepting thoughts without fusion or judgement.

safetyGuidance: OCD is a treatable medical condition, and therapies such as ERP (Exposure and Response Prevention) are highly effective. If you are struggling with OCD patterns, please consider reaching out to a mental health professional who has training in OCD and ERP treatment. You are not your thoughts, and there is skilled help available to support your recovery.
